verdicts.flaw_description: The purchase counts 'cover the sessions that signed in, and a quarter of each segment never signed in', so the 4-7 percent lift is measured on a narrower population (signed-in sessions) than the claim about purchases on the checkout page as a whole; a shift in who signs in would produce the same numbers.

'Pollen and airborne irritants in each group's district fell by half from the previous quarter, and every group lived and slept in unfiltered district air' - a named alternative cause that changed between the compared quarters and demonstrably reached every one of the four groups, so the 4-7 fewer attacks cannot be attributed to the inhaler.

The abduction averages 'cover the patients who were reassessed at the follow-up clinic, and a quarter of each intake missed the follow-up clinic', so the 9-16 degree gains describe only the three quarters who came back, a narrower and plausibly better-recovering group than the intakes the claim is about.

The defect rates 'cover the boards that reached the grading stage, and about a tenth of each run's boards were scrapped before grading' - the boards most likely to be defective are excluded from the denominator and numerator, so the 4-7 percent drop is measured on a narrower, pre-filtered population than the claim about board defects.
